items.followUp: State the Associative Law of Boolean algebra.

rubric.why: Checks the defining idea of commutativity.
rubric.description: States that changing the order of operands does not change the result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this idea, expressed in words or symbols.

rubric.why: Checks the Boolean expressions for the law.
rubric.description: Gives the commutative identities for OR and AND.

modelAnswer: In the commutative law, changing the order of the operands does not change the result.
For Boolean algebra: A + B = B + A and A · B = B · A.

items.followUp: Name the three basic logical operators and state what they do.

rubric.why: Checks what logical operators work with or produce.
rubric.description: States that logical operators work with logical values or produce a true/false result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either acceptable idea.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the basic logical operators.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three.

modelAnswer: Logical operators are used to combine or modify logical conditions and produce a true or false result.
The basic logical operators are AND, OR and NOT.

rubric.why: Checks that topology describes how a network is laid out.
rubric.description: Identifies topology as the arrangement or layout of a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the arrangement/layout idea in a network context.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition includes network devices and their connections.
rubric.description: Mentions the arrangement of devices and their connecting links.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying devices and connections.

modelAnswer: Topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a computer network.
It describes how the devices and their communication links are connected.

rubric.why: Checks the number of devices involved in a point-to-point connection.
rubric.description: States that the connection is between two devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two endpoints.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of the connection.
rubric.description: States that a dedicated link is used for communication between the two devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the dedicated-link idea.

modelAnswer: A point-to-point connection provides a direct connection between two devices.
The link is dedicated to communication between those two devices.

items.followUp: What is a MAC address, and what is it used for?

rubric.description: States that an IP address identifies a device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the device or network connection.

rubric.why: Checks what kind of address an IP address is.
rubric.description: Identifies an IP address as a numerical Internet Protocol address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a numerical address or naming Internet Protocol.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a numerical Internet Protocol address assigned to a device on a network.
It identifies the device so that it can communicate with other devices.

items.followUp: Define the receiver in a data communication system.

rubric.why: Checks the sender's role in communication.
rubric.description: Identifies the sender as the source or origin of the data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the sender as the source.

rubric.description: States that the sender sends or transmits data or a message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the sending/transmitting action.

modelAnswer: The sender is the source or origin of a message in a data communication system.
It sends or transmits the message to the receiver.

items.followUp: Write the HTML tags used to create an ordered list and an unordered list.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the two principal list types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of the third HTML list type.
rubric.description: Names the definition or description list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this list type.

modelAnswer: The types of lists in HTML are ordered lists, unordered lists and definition (description) lists.
They are created using the <ol>, <ul> and <dl> tags, respectively.

items.followUp: Describe star and mesh network topologies.

rubric.why: Checks the main structure of bus topology.
rubric.description: States that devices connect to a single main cable or backbone.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the shared main-cable arrangement.

rubric.why: Checks how devices attach in a bus topology.
rubric.description: Explains that all devices are connected to the bus cable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the devices' connection to the bus.

rubric.why: Checks the defining shape of ring topology.
rubric.description: States that devices form a closed loop or ring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the loop arrangement.

rubric.why: Checks how each device connects in a ring topology.
rubric.description: States that each device connects to its neighbouring device(s) in the ring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the neighbouring-device connection.

modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all devices are connected to one main cable called the bus or backbone.
Data travels along this shared cable to the connected devices.
In a ring topology, each device is connected to its neighbouring device(s), forming a closed loop.
Data travels from one device to the next around the ring.
